method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5) 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism' (18 March 2019), 22 claims; LICENCE: © Medical Journal of Australia / AMPCo (free to read; the MJA copyright policy forbids reproduction without written consent) (read at https://www.mja.com.au/journal/copyright (the article page links 'Copyright and linking policy'; free-to-read full text retrieved 2026-09-23)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830) 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism' (published 2 October 2020), 12 claims; LICENCE: No licence or copyright statement in the PMC record (efetch JATS has no <license> and is abstract-only); free to read on PMC. Treated as all rights reserved (American Society of Hematology). (read at NCBI PMC efetch JATS for PMC7556153 (Europe PMC returned 500) and the PMC article page, from which the full text was read). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every edition 1.0 claim (S1, THANZ 2019) unchanged and adds S2, the ASH 2020 GRADE guideline on treating DVT and PE, for home treatment, thrombolysis and catheter therapy, IVC filters, length of treatment, reduced-dose DOACs and recurrent VTE. Cancer-associated VTE is in a separate ASH guideline that was not used.

claims.claim: **VTE symptoms are non-specific: only about 20% of suspected cases are confirmed,** so actively seek the diagnosis and confirm it with imaging; misdiagnosis in either direction does harm.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wells or Geneva scores must be paired with D-dimer; neither alone can safely rule out VTE.** These rules are for outpatients and emergency departments, not inpatients. (GRADE strong, high)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PERC can rule out PE without more tests in patients under 50 when the expected PE rate is below 15%,** which applies in most Australian and New Zealand EDs; a positive PERC needs further work-up.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A negative D-dimer with a non-high clinical probability avoids imaging; a positive D-dimer alone proves nothing,** since it rises with cancer, inflammation, infection, trauma and pregnancy.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **DVT: a single negative ankle-to-groin duplex ultrasound generally excludes DVT.** A single repeat scan 3–6 months later, before stopping anticoagulation, gives a baseline for future symptoms; repeated scans without symptoms do not help.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PE: CTPA is the preferred test** (GRADE strong, high); VQ scanning suits renal impairment and is preferred in pregnancy. A normal VQ excludes PE, but 27–55% of scans are non-diagnostic and need leg ultrasound or CTPA.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Think of hidden cancer after an unprovoked VTE:** up to 10% are diagnosed with cancer within a year. Examine carefully and do age-appropriate screening; abdominopelvic CT adds nothing.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classify the event as provoked (surgical or non-surgical; transient or persistent) or unprovoked:** this sets recurrence risk and treatment length.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anticoagulate most VTE:** it cuts extension or recurrence by at least 80%. DOACs and warfarin work equally well (GRADE strong, high); DOACs are usually favoured as they need no routine monitoring.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For proximal DVT and PE, choose an oral factor Xa inhibitor (apixaban or rivaroxaban) over dabigatran or warfarin,** because no injectable lead-in is needed. (GRADE strong, high)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No DOACs in pregnancy or breastfeeding: use low molecular weight heparin.** In cancer-associated VTE, edoxaban or rivaroxaban match dalteparin for efficacy but bleed more, so they can be considered case by case.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat at home when you can (ASH, conditional):** for uncomplicated DVT, and for PE at low risk of complications (PESI or simplified PESI can help pick these patients but do not replace judgement). Admit instead for another reason needing hospital, no support at home, inability to pay for medicines or poor adherence; limb-threatening DVT, high bleeding risk, IV analgesia and submassive or massive PE may also need hospital.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **ASH favours a DOAC over a vitamin K antagonist (conditional, moderate certainty)** but may not apply with creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min, liver disease of moderate or greater severity, or antiphospholipid syndrome. **ASH names no preferred DOAC:** choose by need for parenteral lead-in, once- or twice-daily dosing, cost, kidney function, CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein interactions and cancer.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Proximal DVT: anticoagulation alone for most rather than adding thrombolysis (ASH, conditional).** Consider thrombolysis for limb-threatening DVT (phlegmasia cerulea dolens) or for selected younger patients at low bleeding risk with iliac and common femoral vein clot; it should be rare below the common femoral vein. If thrombolysing extensive DVT, prefer catheter-directed to systemic.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **PE with haemodynamic compromise: thrombolyse, then anticoagulate (ASH, strong despite low certainty).** Submassive PE (RV dysfunction on echo or biomarkers without compromise): anticoagulate alone, watch closely for deterioration, and reserve thrombolysis for younger low-bleeding-risk patients or those with cardiopulmonary disease likely to decompensate. For PE, systemic thrombolysis is preferred to catheter-directed, except in experienced centres for higher bleeding risk.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No IVC filter on top of anticoagulation (ASH, conditional)** for proximal DVT with significant cardiopulmonary disease or PE with haemodynamic compromise. If anticoagulation is contraindicated, a retrievable filter may be placed and removed once anticoagulation can start (consistent with S1).
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Proximal DVT or PE: at least 3 months for everyone.** If the cause was major surgery or trauma that has resolved, stop at 3 months. (GRADE strong)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unprovoked, or provoked by a transient non-surgical factor: treat 3–6 months, then decide whether to extend.** Recurrent events (two or more), active cancer or antiphospholipid syndrome warrant extended anticoagulation.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Distal DVT:** anticoagulation benefit is uncertain; two duplex scans over 2 weeks is a reasonable alternative, especially with high bleeding risk. Most distal DVT is treated for 6–12 weeks, and 6 weeks if a major provoking factor has resolved.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Extending beyond 3 months** lowers recurrence by at least 80% during treatment, for a major bleeding risk under 1% a year; the benefit ends when treatment stops. Weigh bleeding against recurrence, with the patient's preference.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For extended therapy, consider a lower DOAC dose:** apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily works as well as 5.0 mg twice daily beyond 6 months, and rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily as well as 20 mg once daily. Either DOAC dose is preferred over warfarin. Avoid aspirin (100 mg daily) unless anticoagulation is impossible: it prevents far less recurrence yet bleeds like rivaroxaban 10 mg. (GRADE strong, high)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrence predictors that drive most decisions:** unprovoked or persistent-factor events (vs surgical), PE or proximal DVT (vs distal), prior VTE, and male sex.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bleeding risk:** active or recent (under 30 days) bleeding usually rules out anticoagulation. Other predictors: prior bleeding (especially on anticoagulants), a bleeding lesion such as peptic ulcer, surgery in the last 14 days, active cancer and severe kidney disease.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ASH primary treatment: 3–6 months rather than 6–12 months** whatever the trigger (transient, chronic or none; conditional, moderate certainty). A longer first phase can be justified where a chronic risk factor is expected to improve, such as mobility with rehabilitation.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **ASH then advises indefinite antithrombotic therapy after unprovoked VTE, or VTE with a chronic risk factor,** rather than stopping (conditional, moderate), unless bleeding risk is high. VTE from a transient factor usually stops after primary treatment. (S1 instead treats unprovoked VTE for a fixed first period and then decides whether to extend.)
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **For unprovoked VTE, do not routinely use prognostic scores, D-dimer or ultrasound for residual clot to decide duration (ASH, conditional, very low certainty);** they may help when the patient is undecided or the balance is unclear.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Long-term prevention after primary treatment (ASH):** an anticoagulant rather than aspirin (conditional); on warfarin, target INR 2.0–3.0 rather than 1.5–1.9 (strong); on a DOAC, standard or reduced dose, such as apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily or rivaroxaban 10 mg once a day (conditional).
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Recurrence on warfarin despite a therapeutic INR: switch to low molecular weight heparin rather than a DOAC and look for a cause (ASH, conditional);** a DOAC is reasonable if the INR was poorly controlled.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A second VTE (ASH):** recurrent unprovoked VTE warrants indefinite therapy (strong). A new transient-factor event after an earlier unprovoked or chronic-factor VTE: continue indefinitely; after an earlier transient-factor VTE: stop after primary treatment (both conditional).
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Aspirin taken for stable cardiovascular disease: usually pause it while anticoagulated (ASH, conditional),** after reviewing why it was started; except soon after an acute coronary event or a coronary intervention.
claims.locator: Ortel TL, Neumann I, Ageno W, et al., American Society of Hematology (ASH), Blood Advances 4(19):4693-4738 (doi 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001830), 'American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: treatment of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism', published 2 October 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7556153/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Do not test routinely for inherited thrombophilia:** factor V Leiden and prothrombin gene heterozygosity change neither duration nor family advice. Testing for antiphospholipid syndrome after unprovoked VTE is reasonable. (GRADE strong, moderate)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspect CTEPH if breathlessness persists over the 2 years after PE** (incidence 3.4%): arrange a VQ scan and echocardiogram. Untreated, 5-year survival is 30%.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Post-thrombotic syndrome affects one in three after DVT;** anticoagulation does not prevent it, and compression stockings are for symptom relief of swelling and pain only.
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Thrombolysis (or an alternative) is for massive, haemodynamically unstable PE;** invasive clot removal otherwise has a limited role. An IVC filter is only for acute VTE with an absolute contraindication to anticoagulation, not for anticoagulated patients. (GRADE strong)
claims.locator: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (THANZ), Medical Journal of Australia 210(5), 'New guidelines from the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand for the diagnosis and management of venous thromboembolism', 18 March 2019, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2019/210/5/new-guidelines-thrombosis-and-haemostasis-society-australia-and-new-zealand, retrieved 2026-09-23
